title: Fix blending in spherical cubic interpolation when from vs to has 180deg gap
body: - Prerequisite / Follow up https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123835 ## What problem(s) does this PR solve? - Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86003 as more stable ## Additional information Currently cubic interpolation blends the expmap results of from and to using slerp with Quaternions. However, if spherical cubic interpolation causes a large overshoot, and there is a gap of 180 degrees or more between rotation result in the expmap of "from" and "to" when converted back to quaternions, the direction of the slerp blend will be inverted. Using slerpni allows gaps up to 360 degrees, but theoretically, cases with gaps exceeding 360 degrees can still occur. This issue becomes prominent when there is a large rotation with a short key, followed by a large keyframe interval. **Test project:** [compare-makima.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32772536/compare-makima.zip) **Linear:** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07cfdaef-8ba4-4422-9c9a-a4e53d00c84c **Cubic (broken):** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb435f59-c4c1-4c88-a575-6290743173cb **Makima (broken):** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7778f22-d314-4af7-a5bc-2aa8c712edd4 Instead of slerp quaternions that have lost angle information beyond 360 degrees due to re-conversion from expmap, this PR solves the problem of inversion by directly blending the expmap results with using the inverse Jacobian matrix to align the expmap space (similar math was used in JacobianIK). By https://arxiv.org/html/1812.01537#A2.E144: > Elementary Jacobian blocks Since our defined derivatives map tangent vector spaces, and these spaces coincide for the 3D rotation manifolds of S3 and SO(3), i.e., 𝜽=Log(𝐪)=Log(𝐑), it follows that the Jacobians are independent of the representation used (𝐪 or 𝐑). **Cubic (fixed):** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eca2b8fb-acbf-4adf-8773-0ac538a29445 **Makima (fixed):** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c5fa2ba-41b6-425a-ba02-61ea0c0ccc64 The angles just on the keyframe is still kept, However, there is a very slight change in the cubic-interpolated curve (Since the matching of the expmap space by the inverse right Jacobian matrix is an approximation. Although, the difference is less than 1 degree in most cases), which might break compatibility, but I consider it insignificant enough to be ignored. Also includes a fix for an issue with `Quaternion::log()` that causes an error when rotation is extremely small.
